questions.title: Garwood exact interval for a Poisson exposure rate in R
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation grounded in F. Garwood, Fiducial Limits for the Poisson Distribution, Biometrika 28(3-4), 1936, 437-442, DOI 10.1093/biomet/28.3-4.437. Let independent counts over known positive exposures have Poisson means lambda times exposure, so their aggregate count Y over total exposure T>0 is Poisson(lambda T). For confidence level 1-alpha, develop one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX derivation of the equal-tailed Garwood interval by inverting Poisson tails and establishing the Poisson-Gamma-chi-square identities. Derive L=0 for Y=0 and L=qchisq(alpha/2,2Y)/(2T) otherwise, U=qchisq(1-alpha/2,2(Y+1))/(2T), and the MLE Y/T. Prove frequentist coverage is at least 1-alpha while explaining discreteness and conservatism; establish endpoint ordering, the zero-count boundary, exposure-scale equivariance, count monotonicity, and confidence-level nesting. The required model-authored artifact is est_poisson_garwood_rate and must implement the frozen run_estimator(request) contract as R source using language=r, execution_profile=scientific_wasm, and only declared base/stats dependencies. Do not substitute Python. Exploratory computation may diagnose identities. A separately frozen confirmatory simulation must also be model-authored R source and compare empirical coverage with independently enumerated exact coverage at predeclared low, moderate, and high expected counts using Monte Carlo uncertainty. Simulation supports implementation behavior and is not a proof. Source replication and novelty are not applicable. Lean formalization is not applicable to this focused nonformal R capability task.

source.title: Fiducial Limits for the Poisson Distribution
source.author: F. Garwood

request_fields.name: count
request_fields.meaning: The aggregate observed Poisson count Y.
request_fields.edge_cases: Zero is allowed; reject logical values, fractional values, negative values, nonfinite values, and nonscalars rather than coercing them.

request_fields.name: exposure
request_fields.meaning: The known strictly positive finite aggregate exposure T.
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject logical, nonnumeric, nonfinite, zero, negative, and nonscalar values.

request_fields.name: confidence_level
request_fields.shape: one finite scalar strictly between zero and one
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject logical, nonnumeric, nonfinite, zero, one, out-of-range, and nonscalar values.

response_fields.name: mle_rate
response_fields.meaning: The Poisson exposure-rate maximum likelihood estimate Y/T.
response_fields.edge_cases: Equals zero when count is zero.

response_fields.name: lower_rate
response_fields.meaning: The lower equal-tailed Garwood confidence endpoint for lambda.
response_fields.edge_cases: Defined as zero when count is zero.
response_fields.normalization: For positive count, the alpha/2 chi-square quantile with 2*count degrees of freedom divided by 2*exposure.

response_fields.name: upper_rate
response_fields.meaning: The upper equal-tailed Garwood confidence endpoint for lambda.
response_fields.edge_cases: Remains positive when count is zero.
response_fields.normalization: The 1-alpha/2 chi-square quantile with 2*(count+1) degrees of freedom divided by 2*exposure.

invariants.meaning: Independent Poisson counts with means lambda times their exposures aggregate to a Poisson count with mean lambda times total exposure, so only total count and exposure enter the interval.
Every admitted request returns lower_rate <= mle_rate < upper_rate, with equality between lower_rate and mle_rate only at count zero.
At count zero, lower_rate and mle_rate are zero while upper_rate is the exact positive one-sided tail inversion at the requested two-sided level.
For fixed count and confidence level, multiplying exposure by c>0 divides both endpoints and the MLE by c.
For fixed count and exposure, increasing the confidence level cannot increase the lower endpoint or decrease the upper endpoint.
For fixed exposure and confidence level, both Garwood endpoints and the MLE are nondecreasing in the observed count.

empirical_claims.meaning: At each frozen Poisson rate and exposure, empirical interval coverage is compatible with independently enumerated exact coverage up to declared Monte Carlo uncertainty.
Independently enumerated exact coverage is at least the requested confidence level; empirical fluctuation is not itself used to prove this property.
Every confirmatory setting binds the exact frozen rate, exposure, confidence level, seed, and precision-driven replicate count before outcomes and invokes the accepted estimator without rewriting it.
